sourceEvidence.label: Work Assistant agent and archive boundaries

assessment.summary: A broker boundary can prevent routine cloud-model exposure while preserving reversible local drafts.

nonNegotiables: Unknown aliases fail closed during restoration.
Privacy mode and sender action are visible in every agent payload.
assumptions: No measured latency or memory budget was supplied.

opportunities.title: Separate clear mail from the agent boundary
opportunities.summary: Move pseudonymization and restoration into an isolatable local broker.
opportunities.diagnosis: The current MCP process can read and return the same clear archive that it is meant to protect.

evidence.claim: Agent tools return clear addresses, subjects and message bodies.
The archive stores normalized clear payloads for local operation.
An inline mapper cannot protect against an agent with direct filesystem access to the archive and key.

desiredInvariants: The agent-facing process cannot read the clear archive or alias key.
Every protected entity has a stable workspace-local alias and authenticated encrypted mapping.
Restoration accepts only aliases issued by the same vault.
Selective sender rules are deterministic and disclosed in output metadata.

options.title: Inline pseudonymization filter
options.summary: Filter responses inside the existing MCP process.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Routine MCP responses are filtered, but filesystem authority remains.

tradeoffs.assessment: Reduces accidental payload exposure but is bypassable by direct file access.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test MCP payloads and attempt direct archive reads from the agent context.

tradeoffs.assessment: Adds local matching and vault lookups.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark synthetic messages by size and entity count.

tradeoffs.assessment: Keeps a bounded alias index in memory.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak RSS with large synthetic contact sets.

tradeoffs.assessment: Unknown aliases can fail before local draft creation.

residualRisks: Agent shell access can bypass the filter.

workPackages: Add policy, vault and response filtering.
acceptanceCriteria: Protected entities do not appear in MCP results.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Set privacy mode to off and revert the filter.

options.title: Isolated local broker
options.summary: A trusted broker owns clear data and exposes only policy-filtered operations to the MCP gateway.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The raw MCP path is replaced by a safe broker protocol.
The archive remains clear locally but leaves the agent-readable workspace.

tradeoffs.assessment: Removes clear archive and mapping authority from the agent process when deployed with OS isolation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Attempt raw file and broker API access from the agent sandbox.

tradeoffs.assessment: Adds local IPC plus matching and authenticated encryption.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark direct versus broker list/get/draft paths.

tradeoffs.assessment: Runs one additional small process and alias cache.
Broker availability becomes a prerequisite, but fail-closed behavior is clearer.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test restart, stale endpoints and interrupted vault writes.

tradeoffs.assessment: Requires process supervision and data-directory isolation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test documented Windows, macOS, Linux and container setup paths.

tradeoffs.assessment: MCP callers must move to the broker protocol.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run compatibility tests for all tool contracts.

residualRisks: Content not matched by structured fields, patterns or the entity registry may remain identifying.

workPackages: Move MCP tools to broker client.
acceptanceCriteria: The gateway has no raw archive API.
Alias restoration occurs only in the broker.
migrationNotes: Start in selective mode or off for existing installations.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Stop the broker and restore the previous MCP command while retaining the archive backup.

options.title: Local-model-only processing
options.summary: Keep model inference on the same trusted device instead of transforming cloud payloads.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Cloud egress is removed, but local process access still needs governance.

tradeoffs.assessment: Avoids routine cloud disclosure but retains local model access to clear data.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Verify network isolation and model runtime permissions.

tradeoffs.assessment: Depends on device and model size.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark target hardware and representative tasks.

tradeoffs.assessment: Local inference can require substantial RAM.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak unified memory on supported devices.

tradeoffs.assessment: Removes cloud dependency but adds local runtime constraints.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test offline operation and model startup recovery.

tradeoffs.assessment: Requires model distribution and hardware qualification.

tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare task quality and tool compatibility.

residualRisks: A local model can still expose data through logs or plugins.

acceptanceCriteria: No model traffic leaves the device.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Return to the broker-backed cloud model surface.

opportunities.recommendation: Use the isolated broker when agents may use cloud models; use local-model-only when hardware and quality are acceptable.

openQuestions: Which OS isolation recipes will be supported in the first release?
